newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps-light ends slip, CFDs dip, fuel holds.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps-light ends slip, CFDs dip, fuel holds.

text.p: European oil swaps were mostly battered lower on Wednesday as the front end of the energy complex came under pressure.
Brent CFDs dipped by several cents a barrel but the main losers were gasoline and naphtha which were off $2-3 a tonne. Fuel looked steady, but quiet.
Brent CFDs for the balance of this week were pegged at -41 cents under July compared with -37 cents while next week June 9-13 was also down at -40 cents against July compared with -34 on Tuesday.

Before crude's slide down a June 9-13 CFD was done at -33 cents under July and a June 15-20 was done at -39 cents under August. Subsequent CFDs for June 9-13 were done twice at July -40 cents. A 16-20 June CFD was also traded at August -41 cents.
Gasoline swaps fell by over $3 a tonne as the market tracked a weaker NYMEX contract that was down 1.74 cent at 61.25 cents a gallon on July.
Traders said June gasoline was around $205.50 from $209 while July retained its $6 backwardation.

"At one point the backwardation widened to $8-10, but it then closed a bit," said one dealer. A June swap traded in the morning at $209.75 which was broadly in line with contemporary physical levels. Barges went at $211 and $209.50 earlier in the day before losing ground.
Physical gasoline was seen fixed transatlantic and a cargo was thought sold today at July NYMEX -6.25 cents.

Heavy fuel was done but on a private basis although several dealers commented they had not seen anything concluded. Swaps levels were pegged a touch lower by 25-50 cents but sellers were reluctant to be drawn too low. Low sulphur swaps also appeared to be holding up well with June heard done at $92.75.

Naphtha, however, was unable to resist the pull downwards and swaps levels were down about $2 a tonne. Activity was quiet for most of the day until a last minute flurry which saw several deals concluded. Most were private, but one was done at $186.75.
